title: fix: honor the processErrors hook in Stats.hasErrors
body:
**Summary**

Fixes #22279.

`Stats.hasErrors()` read `compilation.errors` directly, while `hasWarnings()` goes through `compilation.getWarnings()` — i.e. through the `processWarnings` waterfall hook. Because of that asymmetry, a plugin that filters entries out of the `processErrors` hook was contradicted by `hasErrors()`: `stats.toJson().errors` would be empty while `hasErrors()` still returned `true`.

This routes `hasErrors()` through `getErrors()` (which calls the `processErrors` hook), so it stays symmetric with `hasWarnings()` and reflects the same error list that `toJson()` exposes.

**What kind of change does this PR introduce?**

fix

**Did you add tests for your changes?**

Yes: `test/unitCases/Errors.unittest.js`. Added a `describe("Stats.hasErrors")` block with a control (`hasErrors()` is `true` when the compilation has errors) and the regression case (a `processErrors` tap returning `[]` makes both `toJson().errors` empty and `hasErrors()` `false`). Both tests pass locally.

**Does this PR introduce a breaking change?**

No.

**If relevant, what needs to be documented once your changes are merged or what have you already documented?**

Added a patch changeset; no additional documentation needed.

**Use of AI**

I used Claude to help spot the asymmetry between `hasErrors()` and `hasWarnings()`, confirm that `getErrors()` calls the `processErrors` hook, write the regression tests, and draft this description. I reviewed the fix against the source and ran the tests locally.
